findings.title: No bundle-size or performance budget gate; the analyzer is opt-in only
evidence: apps/web/next.config.mjs:3,57 wraps the config in withBundleAnalyzer({ enabled: process.env.ANALYZE === 'true' })
git grep for performance.budgets / size-limit / bundlewatch returns no config in the repo
findings.impact: Web bundle growth is not measured in CI, so regressions ship unnoticed; the analyzer only runs when a developer sets ANALYZE=true locally.
findings.recommendation: Add a size-limit or Lighthouse-CI/bundle budget to the web CI and fail on threshold, or publish a bundle report on PRs.

findings.title: API routes broadly select all columns (`select("*")`) and pagination is ad hoc
evidence: git grep -c '\.select("\*")' shows all-star selects across many route files (e.g. assets.ts x6, approvals.ts x6, billing.ts x4)
only 24 of 64 files under apps/api/src/routes call .limit(), so list endpoints do not share a pagination contract
findings.impact: Over-fetching increases DB and network cost and couples responses to schema changes; inconsistent pagination risks unbounded result sets as tenant data grows.
findings.recommendation: Project only needed columns, add a shared pagination/limit helper to list endpoints, and add a lint check for bare select("*") on large tables.
